# Data from the table (in millions of dollars)
# Period: December 1941 to December 1942 (inclusive) = 13 months

# Bonds (interest-bearing public debt bonds)
bonds = [
    40000,  # December 1941
    42078,  # January 1942
    44305,  # February 1942
    44847,  # March 1942
    45363,  # April 1942
    48157,  # May 1942
    48776,  # June 1942
    51765,  # July 1942
    53680,  # August 1942
    54413,  # September 1942
    57285,  # October 1942
    57931,  # November 1942
    64868,  # December 1942
]

# Bills and certificates of indebtedness (public CIs and bills that are also public debt interest-bearing)
bills_cis = [
    2002,   # December 1941
    2101,   # January 1942
    2002,   # February 1942
    1652,   # March 1942
    3460,   # April 1942
    3764,   # May 1942
    5604,   # June 1942
    6759,   # July 1942
    8873,   # August 1942
    10829,  # September 1942
    11336,  # October 1942
    12882,  # November 1942
    17161,  # December 1942
]

# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient manually
n = len(bonds)
mean_x = sum(bonds) / n
mean_y = sum(bills_cis) / n

# Calculate numerator: sum of (x - mean_x) * (y - mean_y)
numerator = sum((bonds[i] - mean_x) * (bills_cis[i] - mean_y) for i in range(n))

# Calculate denominator: sqrt(sum((x - mean_x)^2) * sum((y - mean_y)^2))
denominator = math.sqrt(sum((bonds[i] - mean_x)**2 for i in range(n)) * sum((bills_cis[i] - mean_y)**2 for i in range(n)))

correlation = numerator / denominator

print(f"Number of data points: {n}")
print(f"Bonds: {bonds}")
print(f"Bills/CIs: {bills_cis}")
print(f"\nMean bonds: {mean_x}")
print(f"Mean bills/CIs: {mean_y}")
print(f"\nPearson correlation coefficient: {correlation}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places: {round(correlation, 3)}")
EOF
